title: AlphaGenome 2 Brings Single-Cell Precision to Human Regulatory Genomics
whyItMatters: Trained on 100M+ individual cell profiles across 68 tissues, AlphaGenome 2 nearly doubles cell-type-specific causal DNA variant discovery and generalizes zero-shot to new experiments.
summary: Google DeepMind’s AlphaGenome 2 upgrades genomic variant modeling from bulk tissue averages to conditional single-cell precision. Taking a 1-million-letter DNA sequence alongside a target cellular context, it predicts gene expression, histone marks, chromatin accessibility, and DNA methylation—nearly doubling detection of gene-expression-linked variants in specific immune cell types and letting researchers upload their own single-cell RNA-seq profiles without fine-tuning.
technicalHighlights: Trained on >100 million individual cell profiles across 68 human tissues to resolve close cell-type regulatory differences.
Nearly doubled identification of expression-linked variants in specific human cell types (e.g., TenK10K 28 immune cell types).
Zero-shot adaptation to unseen biological states, drug treatments, or disease progression from user-uploaded scRNA-seq data.
caveats: Currently evaluated on DeepMind benchmarks with API access restricted to non-commercial research and private commercial preview; independent clinical validation is pending.

scoreRationale.foundational: Solved the bulk-tissue averaging limitation by conditioning 1 Mb regulatory DNA prediction on single-cell states.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly pinpoints cell-type-specific disease mechanisms and drug targets across human genetics.
scoreRationale.verification: Strong internal and TenK10K benchmark validation; independent peer-reviewed clinical replications pending.
scoreRationale.velocity: Arrived just 16 months after AlphaGenome 1, doubling cell-specific variant resolution.
